record_type_quote: In this paper, we present two studies intended to replicate and extend the work of Pennycook and colleagues (2015) in three distinct ways.

targets.authors: Pennycook, G., Cheyne, J. A., Barr, N., Koehler, D. J., & Fugelsang, J. A.
targets.title: On the reception and detection of pseudo-profound bullshit
targets.evidence_quote: First, we sought to replicate the pattern of correlations between individual differences constructs and PBBS susceptibility reported by Pennycook and colleagues (2015).
targets.outcome_quote: Both of the present studies aimed to (i) replicate the correlates of PPBS profundity ratings reported by Pennycook and colleagues (2015), (ii) determine whether the pattern of associations could be organised in terms of the O/I simplex model identiﬁed by DeYoung and colleagues (2012), and (iii) discover if the individual differences in PPBS profundity ratings were primarily due to differences in discrimination or response bias. On the whole, these goals were successful in both studies.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Authors give an overall successful verdict for the named goals across both studies and describe the original associations as reasonably robust. This overall verdict governs despite some individual nonsignificant associations.

targets.authors: DeYoung, C. G., Grazioplene, R. G., & Peterson, J. B.
targets.title: From madness to genius: The Openness/Intellect trait domain as a paradoxical simplex
targets.evidence_quote: The O/I simplex reported in Study 1 and by DeYoung and colleagues (2012) was approximately replicated, albeit imperfectly, and a simplex model was adequate for describing relations among the O/I constructs.
targets.outcome_quote: The results were also consistent with the DeYoung and colleagues (2012) ﬁnding that the O/I domain is well described by a simplex. In both studies, a simplex model ﬁt the data well, with intelligence at one end, apophenia at the other end, and the remaining constructs falling in between.

reasoning: Two new participant samples retest two published papers. Study 2's repetition of this article's Study 1 is not an additional original.
